body.text: Oṃ namaḥ śrīvajrasattvāya //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>.

body.text:
jyotibhir vijitaṃ yad asya jagatīṃ jiṣṇv antaratvatamo (?)
yac cādvaitadaśārṇasaty api parīṇāmo guṇaughaḥ śriyām /
body.translated_text: Whose radiance has conquered the darkness within the world, and whose transformation, even in the state of non-dual ten-syllabled truth, is an abundance of qualities and glories,

body.text:
yat kāruṇyatarāmṛtārdrahṛdayair uhyanti taṃ vajriṇas
tair etac caritādbhutāni nijadhīdhāmāni dhāvantu vaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whose <s>vajra</s>-holders are borne by hearts moist with the supreme nectar of compassion — may those wondrous deeds of theirs, the abodes of their own wisdom, illuminate you.

body.text: vajrāvalīmaṇḍitamaṇḍaleṣu drāg vajrabhṛc cārucaritram uccaiḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>maṇḍalas</s> adorned with the <s>vajra</s>-garland, may the <s>Vajra</s>-bearer's beautiful conduct be proclaimed aloft,

body.text: tadañcitais tadvacanirmitaughair amogham agryāṃ śriyam ādadhātu //
body.translated_text: And through the hosts of creations fashioned by his words and adorned by him, may he bestow unfailingly the supreme glory.

body.text: iha hi mṛdumadhyakramābhyāṃ subhāvitasamādher adhimātraprajñasya bhagavatā /
body.translated_text: Here, for one whose <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) is well-cultivated through the gentle, middle, and intense stages, and who possesses supreme <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), by the Blessed One:

body.text:
sarvākāravaropetaḥ sphurat saṃhārakārakaḥ /
jhatiti jñānaniṣpanno yogo niṣpanna ucyate //
body.translated_text: Endowed with all excellent aspects, radiantly effecting the dissolution, instantaneously accomplished through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) — this <s>yoga</s> is called <s>niṣpanna</s> (fully accomplished).

body.text: sa hi tvāṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca vajradharatvaṃ prāpayitum abhyutsāhavān skandhadhātvāyatanādikaṃ pratibimbamayaṃ śūnyataikarasaṃ niścinvan / prabhāsvaraṃ praviśya jhatiti saparikarakūṭāgarodaramaṇḍalamāṇḍaleyaparikaritaḥ kuleśabhūṣito
body.translated_text: He, being eager to bring you and all beings to the state of <s>Vajradhara</s>, ascertaining that the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) and so forth are of the nature of reflections and of the single taste of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), entering the <s>prabhāsvara</s> (clear light), instantly becomes surrounded by the retinue of the <s>maṇḍala</s> within the <s>kūṭāgāra</s> (celestial mansion) together with its attendants, adorned as the lord of the <s>kula</s> (family),

body.text: hṛdbījayuktaḥ śūnyatākaruṇaikarasamahāsukhamayaḥ śrīvajrasattvamañjuvajrādirūpo 'parimitatathāgatadevībodhisattvakrodhādīn sphārayet / dharmadeśanādibhir yathābhavyaṃ parahitāni kurvāṇaḥ parapuṇyāvadhiṃ sthāpayan saṃharaṃś cācintya mūrtir udeti //
body.translated_text: endowed with the heart-<s>bīja</s> (seed syllable), of the nature of <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss) which is the single taste of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), in the form of the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>, <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, and others, he emanates immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, goddesses, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Krodhas</s> (wrathful deities), and others. Performing the welfare of others as appropriate through <s>Dharma</s>-teaching and the like, establishing the limit of others' merit, and then dissolving — the inconceivable form arises.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ parikarādiḥ / ārasātalam abhimataprasarā ghanaikasārā jvalantī vajramayī bhūmiḥ kalpāntajvalanavanamayūkhajvālāvalīsīmābandhā / ārasātalam upary atyuccair ghananibuḍajvaladvajraprākārordhve niḥsaṃdhyekakhaṇḍībhūtam upari vajraśarajālādho vajravitānamaṇḍitaṃ jvaladvajrapañjaraṃ tadabhyantarasthitaviśvābjasūryasthapītadakṣiṇāvartabhramaddaśāracakraṃ ca 61 //
body.translated_text: Here is the arrangement of the retinue and so forth: Down to the adamantine ground, extending as far as desired, of dense single essence, blazing, the <s>vajra</s>-ground is bounded by a garland of flame-rays like the fire at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age). Above, rising very high from the ground level, upon the dense, immersed, blazing <s>vajra</s>-rampart, a seamless single mass above, adorned with a canopy of <s>vajra</s>-arrows above and a <s>vajra</s>-awning below, is the blazing <s>vajra</s>-cage. Within it stands a ten-spoked wheel rotating clockwise upon a sun disc placed on a universal lotus, slightly touching the ground. 61.

body.text: tatra pūrvasyām ārāyāṃ yamāntakaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sitaraktamukhaḥ kṛṣṇavajramudgarakhaḍgamaṇikamaladhārī / dakṣiṇasyāṃ prajñāntakaḥ sitaḥ kṛṣṇaraktamukho vajrāṅkitasitadaṇḍāsimaṇipadmadhārī / paścimāyāṃ padmāntako rakto nīlasitāsyo raktapadmāsimaṇicakradhāri / uttarasyāṃ vighnāntakaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sitaraktamukhaḥ karālavajrāsimaṇipadmadhārī / āgneyyāṃ ṭakkirājo nīlaḥ sitaraktāsyo 'ṅkuśakhaḍgamaṇisarojadhārī / nairṛtyāṃ nīladaṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sitaraktāsyo nīladaṇḍakhaḍgamaṇyabjadhārī / vāyavyāṃ mahābalaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sitaraktamukhas triśūlāsimaṇikamaladhārī / aiśānyām acalo nīlaḥ sitaraktāsyaḥ khaḍgavajramaṇipadmadhārī / ūrdhvam uṣṇīṣacakravartī pīto nīlaraktāsyaḥ pītacakrakhaḍgamaṇipadmadhārī / adhaḥ sumbharājo nīlaḥ sitaraktāsyo vajrakhaḍgamaṇikamalabhṛt //
body.translated_text: There, in the eastern spoke, <s>Yamāntaka</s> is black, with white and red faces, holding a black <s>vajra</s>, hammer, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the southern spoke, <s>Prajñāntaka</s> is white, with black and red faces, holding a white staff marked with a <s>vajra</s>, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the western spoke, <s>Padmāntaka</s> is red, with blue and white faces, holding a red lotus, sword, jewel, and wheel. In the northern spoke, <s>Vighnāntaka</s> is black, with white and red faces, holding a fierce <s>vajra</s>, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the southeast, <s>Ṭakkirāja</s> is blue, with white and red faces, holding a hook, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the southwest, <s>Nīladaṇḍa</s> is black, with white and red faces, holding a blue staff, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the northwest, <s>Mahābala</s> is black, with white and red faces, holding a trident, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the northeast, <s>Acala</s> is blue, with white and red faces, holding a sword, <s>vajra</s>, jewel, and lotus. Above, <s>Uṣṇīṣacakravartī</s> is yellow, with blue and red faces, holding a yellow wheel, sword, jewel, and lotus. Below, <s>Sumbharāja</s> is blue, with white and red faces, holding a <s>vajra</s>, sword, jewel, and lotus.

body.text: tatroṣṇīṣaṭakkyacalasumbhā ratnamukuṭino vicitraratnābharaṇā lalitā īṣaddarśitadaṃṣṭrā vigataśmaśravaḥ / tadanye vikṛtarūpāḥ sabhrūbhaṅgāḥ piṅgordhvakeśabhrūśmaśravo vyāvṛttadaṃṣṭrākarālavaktrā lalajjihvā aṭṭāṭṭahāsinaḥ krūrāṣṭanāgabhūṣanā vāmanāḥ pīnās tundilāḥ / daśāpy ete sahāsanair niścalāḥ pratyālīḍhenārāgreṣv īṣadalagnaviśvābjasūryasthāḥ sūryaprabhāḥ saroṣaṇā jvalanto nadanto 'tibhīmāḥ pralayānalapratimamayūkhamukhair aparimitātmakamūrtinirmāṇaiś ca niravadhidhātutrayeṣu vighnaugham akhilam asakṛnnirmūlayantaḥ / ṣaḍbhujāḥ pradhānabhujābhyāṃ svābhaprajñāliṅgitās trimukhāḥ / mukhaṃ tu mūlaṃ śariravarṇaṃ savyavāmaṃ ca yathoktavarṇaṃ pratimukhaṃ raktavartulanetratrayam //
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s>, <s>Ṭakkī</s>, <s>Acala</s>, and <s>Sumbha</s> wear jeweled crowns, are adorned with various jewel ornaments, are graceful, with slightly bared fangs, and are beardless. The others have distorted forms, furrowed brows, tawny upward-standing hair, brows and beards, bared fangs with gaping mouths, lolling tongues, roaring with terrifying laughter, adorned with fierce eight <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), dwarfish, stout, and pot-bellied. All ten together with their seats are immovable, standing in <s>pratyālīḍha</s> (warrior stance) at the tips of the spokes, slightly touching the universal lotus and sun disc, with solar radiance, wrathful, blazing, roaring, exceedingly terrifying, with rays resembling the fire of universal dissolution, through their immeasurable emanated forms continuously uprooting all hosts of obstacles in the three limitless realms. They have six arms, with the principal pair embracing their own <s>prajñā</s> (consort), and three faces. The central face is the color of the body, and the right and left faces are of the colors as stated; each face has three round red eyes.

body.text: cakraṃ cātibhramaṇān niścalopamaṃ nirantaraṃ sphurad anekajvālākalāpaṃ tasya nābhyantare 'dhaḥsūkopari viśālatrikoṇadhavaladharmodayāntaradhaḥkoṇodaragataviśvadalakamalopari viśvakuliśasahitā tadvajrasya digārā yathāyogaṃ vairocanādisamavarṇā vedī ca / tasyāṃ pañcavarṇaratnapariniṣpannaṃ bhāsvanmunīndramaṇḍalacitrāṃśuvyāptasarvadikcakraṃ kūṭāgāram / tasya madhye bhagavān vajrasattvo mañjuvajrarūpaḥ kuṅkumāruṇaḥ kṛṣṇasitasavyetaravadanaḥ pradhānabhujābhyāṃ svābhaprajñāliṅgito 'siśarendīvaracāpadharo ratnamukuṭī vicitraratnādyābharaṇo 'nantābhaḥ / tasya pūrvasyāṃ diśi vairocanaḥ sitaḥ kṛṣṇaraktasavyetaramukhaḥ sitāṣṭāracakrāsimaṇikamaladharaḥ / dakṣiṇasyāṃ ratneśaḥ pīto navāṃśamarakataratnāsicakrapadmadharaḥ / paścimāyām amitābho rakto raktapadmāsimaṇicakradharaḥ / uttarasyām amoghasiddhir haritaḥ khaḍgacakramaṇikamaladharaḥ1 / trayo 'mī kṛṣṇasitasavyetaravaktrāḥ sarve tathāgatā ratnamukuṭino vicitraratnābharaṇāḥ / āgneyyāṃ locanā vairocanasamā / nairṛtyāṃ
body.translated_text: The wheel, due to its extreme rotation, appears as if motionless, continuously emitting clusters of numerous flames. Within its hub, below the spoke-tips and above, within a spacious white triangular <s>dharmodaya</s> (origin of dharma) below, upon a universal-petalled lotus within the lower corner, together with a universal <s>vajra</s>, the spoke-tips of that <s>vajra</s> in the directions are colored like <s>Vairocana</s> and the others as appropriate, and there is a platform. Upon it stands a <s>kūṭāgāra</s> (celestial mansion) fashioned from five-colored jewels, its brilliant rays pervading all the directional circles like the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the Lord of Sages. In its center, the Blessed <s>Vajrasattva</s> in the form of <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, saffron-red in color, with black and white right and left faces, embracing his own <s>prajñā</s> (consort) with his principal pair of arms, holding a sword, arrow, blue lotus, and bow, wearing a jeweled crown, adorned with various jewel ornaments, with boundless radiance. To his east, <s>Vairocana</s> is white, with black and red right and left faces, holding a white eight-spoked wheel, sword, jewel, and lotus. To the south, <s>Ratneśa</s> is yellow, holding a nine-faceted emerald jewel, sword, wheel, and lotus. To the west, <s>Amitābha</s> is red, holding a red lotus, sword, jewel, and wheel. To the north, <s>Amoghasiddhi</s> is green, holding a sword, wheel, jewel, and lotus. These three have black and white right and left faces. All the <s>Tathāgatas</s> wear jeweled crowns and are adorned with various jewel ornaments. In the southeast, <s>Locanā</s> is like <s>Vairocana</s>. In the southwest,

body.text: māmakī akṣobhyasamā raktotpalāsimaṇipadmadharā sarvasādhaneṣu tathā pāṭhāt / vāyavyāṃ pāṇḍarā amitābhasamā / aiśānyāṃ tārā ratneśasamā pītotpalāsimaṇipadmadharā /
body.translated_text: <s>Māmakī</s> is like <s>Akṣobhya</s>, holding a red <s>utpala</s> (lotus), sword, jewel, and lotus — so it reads in all <s>sādhanas</s> (ritual texts). In the northwest, <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> is like <s>Amitābha</s>. In the northeast, <s>Tārā</s> is like <s>Ratneśa</s>, holding a yellow <s>utpala</s> (lotus), sword, jewel, and lotus.

body.text: ato garbhapuṭād bahir āgneyakoṇe rūpavajrā vairocanasadṛśī ratnadarpaṇāsimaṇyabjadharā / nairṛtye śabdavajrā akṣobhyasamā nīlavīṇākṛpāṇamaṇyabjadharā / vāyavye gandhavajrā ratneśasamā pītagandhaśaṅkhāsicakrābjadharā / aiśāne rasavajrā amitābhasadṛśī raktarasapātrāsimaṇicakradharā / prāgdvārottarapārśve sparśavajrā amoghasiddhisamā viśvavarṇavastrāsimaṇyabjadharā / prāgdvāradakṣiṇapārśve dharmadhātuvajrā vajrasattvasamā dhavaladharmodayāsimaṇyabjadharā //
body.translated_text: Then, outside the inner enclosure, in the southeast corner, <s>Rūpavajrā</s> resembles <s>Vairocana</s>, holding a jeweled mirror, sword, jewel, and lotus. In the southwest, <s>Śabdavajrā</s> is like <s>Akṣobhya</s>, holding a blue <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), dagger, jewel, and lotus. In the northwest, <s>Gandhavajrā</s> is like <s>Ratneśa</s>, holding a yellow incense conch, sword, wheel, and lotus. In the northeast, <s>Rasavajrā</s> resembles <s>Amitābha</s>, holding a red flavor-vessel, sword, jewel, and wheel. On the north side of the eastern gate, <s>Sparśavajrā</s> is like <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>, holding a multicolored cloth, sword, jewel, and lotus. On the south side of the eastern gate, <s>Dharmadhātuvajrā</s> is like <s>Vajrasattva</s>, holding a white <s>dharmodaya</s> (origin of dharma), sword, jewel, and lotus.

body.text: etā mañjuvajrādidevatās trivadanāḥ ṣaḍbhujāḥ / ādyacihnadvayaṃ savyābhyām aparadvayaṃ vāmābhyāṃ dadhānāḥ / sarvatra mūlamukhaṃ śariravarṇam eva / pūrvādidvāreṣu yamāntakaprajñāntakapadmāntakāmṛtakuṇḍalayaḥ //
body.translated_text: These deities beginning with <s>Mañjuvajra</s> have three faces and six arms. They hold the first pair of emblems with the right hands and the second pair with the left hands. In every case the central face is the color of the body itself. At the eastern and other gates are <s>Yamāntaka</s>, <s>Prajñāntaka</s>, <s>Padmāntaka</s>, and <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalin</s>.

body.text: atra mañjuvajravairocanadaśadevyaś candreṣu vajraparyaṅkiṇo 'nye sūryeṣu candrasūryataleṣu viśvapadmāni / tathāgatāḥ pradhānabhujābhyāṃ svābhaprajñāliṅgitā devyas tu svābham upāyam //
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, <s>Vairocana</s>, and the ten goddesses sit in <s>vajraparyaṅka</s> (vajra cross-legged posture) on moon discs; the others sit on sun discs. Upon the moon and sun discs are universal lotuses. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> embrace their own <s>prajñā</s> (consort) with their principal pair of arms, while the goddesses embrace their own <s>upāya</s> (male consort).

body.text: kulādhipatis tu śirasi mañjuvajrāditathāgatamāmakīśabdavajrārakṣācakragatāṣṭakrodhānām akṣobhyaḥ / locanārūpavajrāyamāntakānāṃ vairocanaḥ / gandhavajrāyā ratneśaḥ / pāṇḍarārasavajrāpadmāntakānām amitābhaḥ / tārāsparśavajrayor amoghasiddhiḥ / dharmadhātuvajrāyā vajradharaḥ / akṣobhya ity anye //
body.translated_text: As for the family lord upon the head: for <s>Mañjuvajra</s> and the other <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Śabdavajrā</s>, and the eight <s>Krodhas</s> (wrathful deities) stationed in the protective circle, it is <s>Akṣobhya</s>. For <s>Locanā</s>, <s>Rūpavajrā</s>, and <s>Yamāntaka</s>, it is <s>Vairocana</s>. For <s>Gandhavajrā</s>, it is <s>Ratneśa</s>. For <s>Pāṇḍarā</s>, <s>Rasavajrā</s>, and <s>Padmāntaka</s>, it is <s>Amitābha</s>. For <s>Tārā</s> and <s>Sparśavajrā</s>, it is <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>. For <s>Dharmadhātuvajrā</s>, it is <s>Vajradhara</s>. Others say <s>Akṣobhya</s>.

body.text: vajrasattvo 'treṣadraktānuviddhasitavarṇo nīlaraktasavyetaravaktraḥ pradhānabhujābhyāṃ svābhaprajñāliṅgito nīlavajrāsimaṇikamaladhārī viśvapadmacandrāsanaś candraprabho vajraparyaṅkī ratnamukuṭī ratnābharaṇo 'kṣobhyamudritaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrasattva</s> here is white tinged slightly with red, with blue and red right and left faces, embracing his own <s>prajñā</s> (consort) with his principal pair of arms, holding a blue <s>vajra</s>, sword, jewel, and lotus, seated on a universal lotus and moon disc, with lunar radiance, in <s>vajraparyaṅka</s> (vajra cross-legged posture), wearing a jeweled crown, adorned with jewel ornaments, bearing the seal of <s>Akṣobhya</s>.

body.text: iha mañjuvajrasya stanāntare samayasattvasadṛśaṃ jñānasattvaṃ taddhṛccandre khaḍgamuṣṭicandrasthaṃ maṃbījam / śāśvataratneśāmitābhāmoghasiddhyakṣobhyānāṃ hṛdi cihne yathāyogaṃ candre sūrye vā vuṃ āṃ jrīṃ khaṃ hūṃ / locanādidevīnāṃ Ioṃ māṃ pāṃ tāṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ khaṃ raṃ / krodhānāṃ hūṃ / sarvadevatānāṃ hṛdayamantrā vajrāvalyāṃ uktāḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, at the chest of <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, is the <s>jñānasattva</s> (wisdom-being) resembling the <s>samayasattva</s> (pledge-being). On a moon disc at his heart is the <s>bīja</s> (seed syllable) <s>maṃ</s>, placed upon a sword-hilt and moon. For <s>Ratneśa</s>, <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>, and <s>Akṣobhya</s>, who are eternal, at the heart upon their respective emblems, on a moon or sun disc as appropriate, are <s>vuṃ</s>, <s>āṃ</s>, <s>jrīṃ</s>, <s>khaṃ</s>, <s>hūṃ</s>. For the goddesses beginning with <s>Locanā</s>: <s>loṃ</s>, <s>māṃ</s>, <s>pāṃ</s>, <s>tāṃ</s>, <s>jaḥ</s>, <s>hūṃ</s>, <s>vaṃ</s>, <s>hoḥ</s>, <s>khaṃ</s>, <s>raṃ</s>. For the <s>Krodhas</s> (wrathful deities): <s>hūṃ</s>. The heart-<s>mantras</s> of all the deities are stated in the <s>Vajrāvalī</s>.

body.text: iha niṣpannayoginaś cakṣurādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ jñānasattvapraveśādikaṃ ca noktam // tadantareṇāpy aparimitācintyacakṣurabhijñādiguṇagrāmaramaṇīyamūrter abhīṣṭadevatāyāḥ sakṛd eva supariśuddhasarvākārapariniṣpatter muhur muhur adhimokṣadārḍhyāt / hṛnmantrādikathanaṃ tu kalaśādhivāsanādiṣu prayogārtham // yadā tu madhye 'nyas tathāgato bhavati nāyakas tadā madhyasthitas tasya sthāne tiṣṭhet / amitābhaḥ śubhro 'pi bhavati śuklā dharmāḥ prakṛtyeti vāgīśasyātra śuklatety ukteḥ // iha vakṣyamāneṣu ca mandaleṣu yasyā māṇḍaleyadevatāyā mukhyato yatsthānam ucyate tasmin saiva pradhānatayā maṇḍaleśabhimukhī / tadāliṅgitā tu tadabhimukhy eva parasthānagamanāt //
body.translated_text: Here, for the fully accomplished <s>yogin</s>, the empowerment of the eyes and other senses, the entry of the <s>jñānasattva</s> (wisdom-being), and so forth are not stated. Even without that, since the form of the chosen deity — delightful with its host of qualities such as immeasurable and inconceivable divine eye and <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) — is perfectly accomplished in all aspects at once through the firmness of repeated conviction, the statement of heart-<s>mantras</s> and the like is for the purpose of application in rituals such as <s>kalaśādhivāsana</s> (consecration of the vase). When another <s>Tathāgata</s> is the central lord, the one who would stand in the center should take that one's place. <s>Amitābha</s> may also be white, since it is said 'dharmas are pure by nature' and since it is stated here by <s>Vāgīśvara</s> that 'the white one.' In the <s>maṇḍalas</s> to be described hereafter, whichever <s>maṇḍala</s> deity is stated as principally belonging to a particular position, that deity faces the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s> in that position as the principal one. The one embraced by that deity also faces that same direction, since she accompanies him to the other position.

body.text: atra kūṭāgārasya vajrabhūmyādiparito vajrapañjaraṃ rakṣācakraṃ dharmodayā ceti trayaḥ parikarāḥ / tatra vajrapañjaraṃ vakṣyamānānām api sarveṣāṃ kūṭāgārāṇāṃ rakṣācakraṃ
body.translated_text: Here, surrounding the <s>kūṭāgāra</s> (celestial mansion) from the <s>vajra</s>-ground onward, there are three accessories: the <s>vajra</s>-cage, the protective circle, and the <s>dharmodaya</s> (origin of dharma). Among these, the <s>vajra</s>-cage belongs to all <s>kūṭāgāras</s> that will be described, while the protective circle

body.text: dharmodayā ca keṣāṃcid eveti vakṣyāmaḥ / lekhyakūṭāgārāṇāṃ tu dharmadhātusvarūpadharmodayāyā dharmadhātvantargatasya vā sūcakaṃ likhanam uktaṃ vajrāvalyām // yathā bāhyaṃ tathādhyātmam ity utpannakramamaṇḍalapratipādanākṛtena lokadhātoś cakravāḍasūcakaṃ vajrāvalīlikhanaṃ ca niyamenaiva / naivaṃ rakṣācakram ato na likhyate / vighnanivāraṇaṃ tv anyathā kriyate / api ca śūnyataiva bhagavatī nikhilavighnaughaṃ samūlam unmūlayituṃ prabhavatīti tadadhimokṣadṛḍhatvam evādarotpādanāya rakṣācakralikhanaṃ na varṇitaṃ lekhyamaṇḍaleṣu / bhāvyamaṇḍaleṣu tu kvacid eva tadbhāvanoktā na sarveṣu / vighnaghātānantaraṃ śūnyatāpraveśād bhāvyamaṇḍale 'pi rakṣācakraṃ nāsty ato na likhyate caitat / evaṃ tarhi vajraprākāram api cakravāḍasūcakaṃ na likhitavyam / atha kūṭāgārotpattau
body.translated_text: and the <s>dharmodaya</s> belong to only some, as we shall explain. For <s>kūṭāgāras</s> that are drawn, it is stated in the <s>Vajrāvalī</s> that the drawing serves as an indicator of the <s>dharmodaya</s> whose nature is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (reality-realm), or of what is contained within the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Just as external corresponds to internal, the drawing of the <s>vajrāvalī</s> (vajra-garland) as an indicator of <s>Cakravāḍa</s> (the world-encircling mountains) is done without exception, this being done in the manner of presenting the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>utpannakrama</s> (generation stage) of the world-realm. The protective circle is not like this, and therefore is not drawn. The removal of obstacles is accomplished by other means. Moreover, <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) itself, the Blessed Lady, has the power to uproot all hosts of obstacles completely — therefore, to generate reverence for the firmness of that conviction, the drawing of the protective circle is not prescribed for drawn <s>maṇḍalas</s>. For visualized <s>maṇḍalas</s>, the visualization of the protective circle is taught in some cases but not all. Since entry into <s>śūnyatā</s> follows immediately after the destruction of obstacles, the protective circle does not exist even in the visualized <s>maṇḍala</s>, and therefore it is not drawn. If so, then the <s>vajra</s>-rampart also, being an indicator of <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, should not be drawn. But at the arising of the <s>kūṭāgāra</s>,

body.text: tad utpadyate / nahi bhagavatā vajraprākārasya dvitīyavārotpattiḥ kvacid uktā //
body.translated_text: it arises together with it. The Blessed One has never stated a second arising of the <s>vajra</s>-rampart anywhere.

body.text: kiṃ vā dvir utpattyā / sakṛd utpannam eva hi vajrabhūbandhaprākārādikaṃ samastasamāropaśūnyatāsvabhāvaṃ māyāmayam avatiṣṭhata eva / vidyamānatve 'pi rakṣācakrasya maṇḍaleṣv alikhanopattir uktaiva / kaiścit tu kvacid rakṣācakram api likhituṃ saṃmanyate //
body.translated_text: What need is there of a double arising? The <s>vajra</s>-ground, rampart, and so forth, once arisen, being devoid of all superimposition, having <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) as their nature, and being illusory, simply remain as they are. Even though the protective circle exists, its non-depiction in the <s>maṇḍalas</s> has already been explained. Some, however, consider it permissible to draw the protective circle in certain cases.

body.text: iti mañjuvajramaṇḍalam // //
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Mañjuvajra</s> <s>maṇḍala</s>.
